claims.statement: For each fixed independence number a, every ordinary tree T with alpha(T)=a has order at most 2a and hence lies in a finite isomorphism-class search domain; furthermore, all original leaves sharing an original support have identical Delta_p(T-v) selector values and identical selected summands, so their full tagged contribution is exactly their multiplicity times the common summand.
claims.scope: Exact fixed-a finite reduction and same-support compression for finite ordinary trees, preserving the strict selector and tagged aggregate. This provides no uniform bound over a and no sign conclusion for the complete sum.
claims.reason: retained: the bipartition order bound proves finite search for each fixed a, and exchanging same-support leaves is an automorphism that preserves the exact selector and both deletion-count sequences. Multiplicity preserves all distinct leaf tags. The result has no uniform bound in a and no aggregate sign consequence.

limitations: The retained statement is parameterwise in a and does not give a finite uniform search domain.
Same-support compression does not control cancellation or compensation between distinct supports.
No exhaustive computation, counterexample, proof of the primary inequality, or imported theorem is established.
